title: Smooth the night light's PWM
story: The virtual night light makes 488 Hz PWM (period 2.048 ms) between 0 and 3.3 V. At 50% duty, a 10 kohm resistor and a capacitor turn it into a steady voltage for an analog dimmer. Choose the capacitor so that after 100 ms the output sits between 1.5 V and 1.8 V and its ripple (measured over the second half of the run) is under 0.25 V.

goals.label: output between 1.5 V and 1.8 V at 100 ms

hints: The settled average is duty x 3.3 V = 1.65 V, but only if the filter has had a few time constants to get there.
Ripple is about 3.3 x 0.5 x 0.5 x 2.048 ms / RC.
Too small a capacitor ripples by volts; too big a one has not charged yet after 100 ms.
